title: U.S. House · Florida's 16th District
area: The Sarasota–Bradenton area on Florida's Gulf Coast, including Sarasota, North Port, and parts of Manatee County, under Florida's 2026 congressional map.

context.text: Florida's U.S. House elections use a new congressional map for 2026; Gov. Ron DeSantis signed the new district boundaries into law on May 4, 2026.

Incumbent Rep. Vern Buchanan (R) did not make the ballot for the 16th District; the seat is open. Sydney Gruters won the Republican primary on August 18, 2026, defeating Eddie Speir and Ed Pope. Kelly Kirschner won the Democratic primary the same day, defeating Tamika Lyles, Jan Schneider, Jonathan Harris, and Glenn Pearson.

summary.text: Kelly Kirschner is a former Mayor and City Commissioner of Sarasota and a nonprofit founder running for the open 16th District seat. He describes himself as a third-generation Floridian and former Peace Corps volunteer.

background.text: Graduated from Cardinal Mooney Catholic High School and Georgetown University (1998); works in higher education administration.
Served as a Sarasota City Commissioner and later as Mayor of Sarasota, where he says he led passage of local campaign finance reforms approved by more than 80% of voters.
Founded a nonprofit that he says helps first-generation students attend top universities debt-free.

priorities.text: Says he is running to end price gouging by oil, electric utility, and grocery companies, hold insurance companies accountable, and invest in affordable energy to lower bills.

Says Congress "just broke that promise" on Medicaid and Medicare, citing loss of healthcare coverage for people in the district, and pledges to restore cuts and protect coverage for pre-existing conditions.
priorities.quote: One in three people in this district depend on Medicaid or Medicare... Congress just broke that promise, stripping healthcare from nearly 280,000 of your neighbors in this district alone.

priorities.text: Says only Congress has the constitutional power to declare war and criticizes Washington leadership for avoiding debate on military engagements.

positions.summary: Pledges to restore recent federal cuts to Medicaid and Medicare and protect coverage for pre-existing conditions.
positions.quote: I am running to restore every cut, protect every patient with a pre-existing condition, and make crystal clear to every hospital along the Gulf Coast: we are not abandoning you.

positions.summary: Says he wants to close loopholes that let corporations and billionaires pay little or no federal tax.
positions.quote: I'm also passionate about fixing the loopholes that allow corporations and billionaires to pay 0 in taxes while our costs continue to go up.

positions.summary: Criticizes recent tariff policy as harmful to Florida small businesses, farmers, and fishermen.
positions.quote: When tariff chaos hammers Florida small and medium-sized businesses, farmers, and fishermen while Wall Street hedges its bets and becomes a casino, that's Washington gambling with someone else's livelihood.

summary.text: Sydney Gruters is a Republican candidate for the open 16th District seat, endorsed by President Trump and running on a platform of lowering costs and border security.

background.text: Has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; limited independently sourced biographical detail is available beyond her campaign materials.

priorities.text: Campaign lists cost-of-living, secure border, inflation, election security, and housing costs as top priorities.
Says she will work with President Trump and ICE on immigration enforcement, and will fight to curb overdevelopment to keep homeownership within reach.

positions.summary: Says she will work with President Trump and ICE to increase immigration enforcement.
positions.quote: Sydney will work with President Trump and ICE to keep our families safe from violent criminals entering our country illegally.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for cutting taxes generally rather than raising them, framed as helping working families keep more of their earnings.
positions.quote: Sydney is ready to cut taxes and fight rising costs so working families can afford gas, groceries, and everyday essentials.

summary.text: Mark Davis, a U.S. Air Force veteran and small-business owner, is running with no party affiliation for Florida's 16th Congressional District.

background.text: Davis served in the U.S. Air Force from 2005 to 2013 and earned a high school diploma from Western High School.
His career experience includes working as a business owner in healthcare.

priorities.text: Describes his campaign as grassroots and not backed by billionaires or political machines.
Says he is focused on affordable healthcare, protecting freedoms, economic security, and restoring truth to government.

positions.quote: I support a single-payer system that puts people before profit and ends the scam of private insurers.

positions.summary: Says he supports both the 2nd Amendment and additional gun-safety laws.
positions.quote: I support the 2nd amendment AND common sense gun laws because kids shouldn’t be getting shot in schools while politicians cash NRA checks.

positions.summary: Says he supports defending bodily autonomy along with voting rights and equal rights.
positions.quote: I believe in protecting voting rights, defending bodily autonomy, and smashing corruption wherever it hides.

record.text: Arrested July 28, 2026 in Manatee County and charged with obstruction of an officer without violence, after deputies said he attempted to enter his home during a court-ordered child-welfare check by the Department of Children and Families despite an order barring him from the house; Davis said the underlying DCF complaint was false and called the incident retaliation for his criticism of President Trump and Gov. Ron DeSantis.
